SEARCH
Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api

Interface RulesEngine<O>

Type Parameters:
O - The output object type to instantiate
All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface RulesEngine<O> extends AutoCloseable
Runs rules against facts: it evaluates each Rule's condition and fires the actions of the rules that match, as its match policy decides. Build one with RulesEngineBuilder, which sets its match policy, expression languages, imports, listeners, limit on compiled copies and run timeout once.

Lifecycle: compile the rules with load(List), then call run(FactStore) or runWithResult(FactStore) as often as needed, from any number of threads. Rules are evaluated in descending priority order; equal priorities keep their list order, and a null priority sorts last. load may be called again at any time to swap in new rules atomically. Close the engine with close() once it's no longer needed.

Implementing: you may implement this interface, for example to decorate an engine or as a test double. Implement load(List), validate(List), runWithResult(FactStore, RunOptions) and rules(); run(FactStore), runWithResult(FactStore) and close() have defaults. A method added in a later 2.x release is a default method, so an existing implementation keeps compiling. RunResult.of(Object, List, List, String) and RuleSetInfo.of(List, String, java.time.Instant) create the values an implementation returns.

  • Method Details

    • load

      void load(List<Rule> ruleList)
      Compiles a rule list and swaps it in for the rules loaded before, if any.
      Parameters:
      ruleList - The list of Rule objects
      Throws:
      RuleCompilationException - if the list contains a null rule; two rules share a name; a condition or action is blank; a rule is written in a language the engine doesn't have; a condition or action has a syntax error its language detects, or is one its language rejects, such as a condition with an assignment; a language throws while creating its compiler, or returns null instead of a compiler or a compiled expression; a LinkageError such as a NoClassDefFoundError is thrown for a class a rule uses, which means the rule is misconfigured rather than the JVM failing; or a declared fact has a name the rules' languages can't refer to. A null rule or a duplicate name is thrown at once. The other problems are collected before the exception is thrown, and failures() lists them: each broken rule, a language that can't create its compiler (once, in place of the first rule that needed it; the rules written in it aren't compiled and get no failure of their own), and each declared fact name the compilers that were created reject. Once the rules compile, an engine built with copiesAtLoad(n) makes its copies of them, and a language that throws while creating or warming up a session for one, or returns null instead of a session, fails the load with this exception, naming the language, on its own.
      IllegalStateException - if the engine is closed; this is checked before anything in the list, so a closed engine throws it even for a list that would fail to load
      NullPointerException - if ruleList itself is null
      Error - a VirtualMachineError other than StackOverflowError thrown while compiling or making copies, also as the cause of another exception, is logged and then rethrown unchanged. So is one a language throws while closing a session or a compiler, once everything being closed has been closed: the first, if there are several. When a load that failed closes what it made, that error is thrown in place of the load's own failure, unless the load failed with a fatal error, which came first and is thrown instead. The error carries the failure it replaces as a suppressed exception; if it can't carry one, as an OutOfMemoryError the JVM throws itself can't, that failure is logged at WARN. When a reload closes the rules it replaced, it is thrown after the new rules were swapped in: they stay loaded, and runs use them. A Throwable that is neither an Exception nor an Error is never fatal: it's handled like an exception from the same place, reported as a RuleCompilationException while compiling or making copies, and logged at WARN while closing.

    • validate

      List<RuleCompilationException> validate(List<Rule> ruleList)
      Compiles a rule list exactly as load(List) would, with this engine's languages, imports, options and declared facts, without loading it, and returns the problems load() would have thrown instead of throwing. The two lists aren't quite the same, and the paragraphs below say how. The rules loaded, if any, are unchanged, and the compiled result is discarded: a later load() compiles the list again. Nothing about the rules is logged, not even a language's compile warnings; a fatal Error is logged at ERROR before it's rethrown, and a compiler that fails to close at WARN, as always.

      One problem this method can't report: it makes no copies. An engine built with copiesAtLoad(n) above zero makes them once the rules compile, and a language that throws while creating or warming up a session for one, or returns null instead of a session, fails that load(), naming the language. With the default copiesAtLoad(0) nothing is outside what it can see.

      The problems come in the order load() finds them: a null entry or a duplicate name, in list order; then each rule that doesn't compile, in priority order, with a language that can't create its compiler in place of the first rule that needed it; then each declared fact name the languages reject. Unlike load(), a null entry or a duplicate name doesn't stop the check: every other rule is still compiled.

      Parameters:
      ruleList - The list of Rule objects
      Returns:
      One exception for each problem found, as load() would have reported it; empty when it finds none
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the engine is closed
      NullPointerException - if the list itself is null
      Error - a VirtualMachineError other than StackOverflowError thrown while compiling, also as the cause of another exception, is logged and then rethrown unchanged. So is one a language throws while closing a compiler, once every compiler created has been closed: the first, if there are several, unless compiling threw a fatal error, which came first and is thrown instead. Either way the problems found aren't returned.

    • run

      default @Nullable O run(FactStore<?> facts)
      Runs the loaded rules against facts.
      Parameters:
      facts - The facts to run the rules against. Any FactStore is accepted, such as a FactMap<Applicant>. The engine reads them through FactStore.asMap().
      Returns:
      The output of the actions of the matching Rule objects, or null if the rule list is empty or no rule matched
      Throws:
      RuleExecutionException - if a condition or action throws; a condition evaluates to null or a non-boolean; an action returns null instead of an ActionResult, or a property it returned can't be set on the output; the output supplier throws or returns null; a language throws or returns null when it creates a session for the run; or more than one rule matches on a unique-match engine, which names them all and belongs to no rule. Also if the run must stop, which is checked while it waits for a compiled copy of the rules, while it reads the engine's rules again after a reload or close() closed the list it had read, between rules and when each condition or action returns, because its thread was interrupted, which keeps the interrupt status set and makes the cause an InterruptedException, or because it passed the deadline a timeout gave it, which makes the cause a TimeoutException. Either belongs to no rule, so getRuleName() is null.
      IllegalArgumentException - if a fact is named output or null, or has a name that the language of a loaded rule can't refer to (a rule list without rules is checked against the engine's default language); if a declared fact has a non-null value that isn't an instance of its declared type or, for a primitive type, of its wrapper or of a wrapper whose primitive Java widens to it; or, with RulesEngineBuilder.requireDeclaredFacts(), if a declared fact is missing or an undeclared one is supplied. Also if a language's check of a fact name fails with any other exception, which becomes the cause.
      IllegalStateException - if load(List) has not been called, or the engine is closed; or if the engine's rule list was closed over and over while the run was borrowing a copy of it, which means an engine invariant has broken rather than that the call was wrong
      NullPointerException - if facts is null
      Error - a VirtualMachineError other than StackOverflowError, wherever it arises (a rule or Java code it calls, the output supplier, an output writer, a language checking a name, creating a session or closing one, or a listener), is rethrown unchanged, also when it arrives as the cause of another exception. A run that gives back an extra copy, made because every kept copy was in use, a copy that couldn't be kept for a later run, or a copy of rules a reload or close() replaced, closes that copy, and the last one to give back a copy of replaced rules closes their compilers too; a run whose new copy was only partly made closes the sessions it made; and a run that fails to get a copy closes the compilers without having held one, if it was the last to use the rules; if its wait for a copy, or for a build slot to make one, was stopped, it has already reported the stop to its listeners. A fatal error from that closing reaches the run: it's thrown even when the rules ran without failing, and in place of a failure of the run that isn't fatal, which it carries as a suppressed exception; if it can't carry one, as an OutOfMemoryError the JVM throws itself can't, that failure is logged at WARN. A fatal error of the run's own came first, and is thrown instead. Every other Error from a rule, the output supplier, an output writer or a language creating a session, including a LinkageError, is reported as a RuleExecutionException; one from a language's check of a fact name as an IllegalArgumentException; one from a listener is logged, and the run goes on; one from closing a session is logged at WARN. A Throwable that is neither an Exception nor an Error is never fatal: wherever it arises, it's handled like an exception from the same place.

    • runWithResult

      default RunResult<O> runWithResult(FactStore<?> facts)
      Runs the rules like run(FactStore), and reports what the run did: the output object, the rules that fired, what each rule's condition evaluated to, the checksum of the rules the run used, and the run's tags and start instant. A caller can record which rules produced a decision, and why the others didn't apply, without a RuleListener.
      Parameters:
      facts - The facts to run the rules against, as run(FactStore) takes them
      Returns:
      What the run did, never null. Its output is null exactly when no rule fired, because the rule list is empty or no condition matched, and its evaluations have one entry per loaded rule.
      Throws:
      RuleExecutionException - as run(FactStore) throws it
      IllegalArgumentException - as run(FactStore) throws it
      IllegalStateException - if load(List) has not been called, or the engine is closed; or if the engine's rule list was closed over and over while the run was borrowing a copy of it, which means an engine invariant has broken rather than that the call was wrong
      NullPointerException - if facts is null

    • runWithResult

      RunResult<O> runWithResult(FactStore<?> facts, RunOptions options)
      Runs the rules like runWithResult(FactStore), with settings for this run only, such as a timeout that replaces the one the engine was built with.

      A timeout's deadline is taken from when this method is called, so waiting for a compiled copy of the rules counts towards it. The engine checks it while waiting, while the run reads the engine's rules again after a reload or close() closed the list it had read, and before and after each condition and each action, so a run stops between rules, and when the condition or action that was running returns; see RulesEngineBuilder.runTimeout(Duration) for what that does and doesn't stop.

      Parameters:
      facts - The facts to run the rules against, as run(FactStore) takes them
      options - The settings for this run; RunOptions.defaults() changes nothing
      Returns:
      What the run did, as runWithResult(FactStore) reports it
      Throws:
      RuleExecutionException - as run(FactStore) throws it, and with a TimeoutException cause if the run passes its deadline, or an InterruptedException cause if its thread is interrupted, which keeps the interrupt status set
      IllegalArgumentException - as run(FactStore) throws it
      IllegalStateException - if load(List) has not been called, or the engine is closed; or if the engine's rule list was closed over and over while the run was borrowing a copy of it, which means an engine invariant has broken rather than that the call was wrong
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • rules

      RuleSetInfo rules()
      Returns the rules the engine has loaded, their checksum and when they were loaded. A run started before a reload finishes with the rules it started with, so compare RunResult.ruleSetChecksum() with RuleSetInfo.checksum() rather than assuming they match.
      Returns:
      The loaded rules, never null. Before the first load(List) it has no rules, the checksum of an empty rule list, and no load time.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the engine is closed

    • close

      default void close()
      Closes the engine, and releases what its expression languages hold for the rules, such as interpreter contexts. A run holding a copy of the rules finishes normally, and so does one waiting for a copy, because a rule list can't close under a run that has begun borrowing from it: the languages' sessions are closed as each run returns, and their compilers after the last one. Afterwards, run(FactStore) and load(List) throw IllegalStateException — as does a run that had read the rules but had not yet begun to borrow a copy when this method closed them, because it reads them again and finds a closed engine. A load() that found the engine open before this method closed it isn't stopped. If it fails, it throws what it would on an open engine, such as RuleCompilationException. If it succeeds, either it swapped its rules in first, and this method closes them like any others, or it finds the engine closed, closes its rules rather than swapping them in, and throws IllegalStateException. Closing an engine that is already closed does nothing.

      A failure to close a session or a compiler is logged at WARN and not thrown, except a fatal Error, which is rethrown unchanged once every idle session, and the compilers if no run holds a copy, has been closed: the first, if there are several. The engine is closed all the same, so closing it again does nothing. A copy a run still holds is closed when the run gives it back, and a fatal error from that reaches the run. By default, this method does nothing.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
